subject: Post-demo: ranking signal taxonomy, auth flow, and canary plan

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: ranking signal taxonomy, auth flow, and canary plan

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to see the Bluebyte search demo and discuss where a neural reranker could lift CTR and conversion for article recommendations. Recap below and a proposed set of next steps so we can get engineering unblocked.

Quick recap of asks we heard:
- You want to preserve existing lexical signals (ES/BM25) and layer a learned reranker on top of candidate lists.
- Important KPIs: CTR -> engagement -> subscription conversion (you care most about downstream conversion lift).
- Security: preference for OIDC SSO for service-to-service; procurement will need a brief compliance packet (SOC2 basics).
- Traffic: peak 200 qps, average 60 qps; critical slices are logged/search and personalized feed.

Attachments: architecture diagram (bluebyte-ranking-arch-v1.png), suggested auth flow (auth-flow.drawio) — both in the Drive folder linked below.

Proposed technical approach and open questions:
1) Candidate generation: keep current ES results as prefilter; we recommend sampling candidate set size = 100 and reranking top_n = 20 as a starting point. Will tune top_k/top_n during eval.
2) Reranker model: run as a re-ranking endpoint (Ranking API). We support streaming and structured outputs; for your use case the endpoint will return scores + optional attribution tokens if you want explainability.
3) Embeddings / vector store: recommend semantic recall via HNSW index (FAISS/HNSW). We can push sample embeddings or you can compute locally.
4) Auth & SDK: two options — sandbox API-key for quick PoC or OIDC with short-lived tokens for production. Which do you prefer for the initial integration?
5) Metrics & evaluation: offline metrics we recommend: NDCG@5/10, MRR@5/10, and simulated CTR uplift using held-out clicks; offline labelling guidance included in the Drive doc. For online: canary A/B with step-up traffic (1% -> 5% -> 20%).
6) Observability / tracing: we’ll include per-request trace-id and token/latency logs; need to agree on retention and PII handling.

Next steps (suggested):
- You share a small sample of 5–10k queries+candidates+labels (or click logs) to run an initial offline run (we can sign an NDA if required).
- Engineering sync: 30-minute technical kickoff next week to walk SDK/auth quickstart and schedule the canary.
- We’ll prepare a short canary plan with SLA rollback thresholds (p95 latency < 200ms incremental, negative CTR lift > -0.5% triggers rollback).

Can you confirm: (a) preferred auth for PoC (API key vs OIDC), (b) who from your infra team should be on the tech kickoff, and (c) an approximate date range for the sample data?

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi and Aditya on the technical details once you confirm.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

We can do an API key for the initial sandbox — that’ll let our infra run smoke tests this week. For production we do prefer OIDC (service account flow) and we’ll need short-lived tokens.

> who from infra should join
I’ll bring Priya (infra lead) and Aaron (search infra). I’ll confirm Aaron’s calendar after this.

> sample data date range
We can extract ~8k recent queries + ES candidate lists and a week of click logs. ETA for that export: EOD next Tuesday (May 25). We’ll scrub PII and provide click counts and dwell-time fields.

A couple of follow-ups from our side: 
- Can you share an estimated ballpark cost delta for running a reranker for our traffic (60 qps avg, 200 qps peak)? A per-1000-token or per-request estimate is fine.
- We currently store embeddings in our own vector index (Elasticsearch vector plugin). Will Redwood accept externally-hosted embedding indices or do we need to push vectors to Redwood?

I attached a brief internal doc on our ranking signals: internal-signals-v2.pdf (uploaded to the Drive link).

Thanks — Evan

Thanks — a few concrete engineering recommendations based on the notes and the sample size (8k):

Evaluation / offline plan:
- Dataset: we’ll use the 8k queries + candidate lists. Hold out 10% for validation, 10% for test; remaining for training when we run a shallow supervised reranker. If human labels are available, prefer graded relevance (0/1/2) for NDCG computation.
- Metrics: primary = NDCG@5 and MRR@10; secondary = CTR-simulated lift and pairwise loss. We’ll also compute calibration and score distributions.
- Candidate sampling: ingest ES candidate list (size variable). If not present, fallback to top-100 prefilter from ES. Start with reranking top_n=20 (this matches your UX constraint). Sweep top_n in {10,20,50} during eval.

Runtime / architecture:
- Flow: (1) prefilter ES -> (2) optional embed similarity filter (HNSW) -> (3) ranking API (batch rerank). We recommend batching requests client-side in groups of 16 for CPU/GPU utilization and 100ms p95 service latency target.
- Batch size / concurrency: for 60 qps avg, a single dedicated lightweight pool with batching=16 and concurrency 8 should be fine; we’ll provide scaling guidance when we run load.
- Top_k tuning guidance: for editorial/product-heavy queries, smaller top_n (10) is often better; for exploratory queries, larger (50) can help recall. Default: top_n=20.

Auth / SDK:
- PoC: API key for sandbox (rotate keys per environment).
- Prod: OIDC with audience/restricted scopes (we support token exchange pattern; Redwood accepts JWT with aud: 'redwood-ranking' and a scope claim). We’ll share a sample token exchange snippet for your infra.

Canary plan (online):
- Step-up: 1% (24h) -> 5% (48h) -> 20% (72h) -> 100% if no regressions.
- Rollback triggers: upstream p95 latency increase > +100ms absolute, negative CTR lift <= -0.5% over baseline, or error rate > 1%.
- Instrumentation: please include trace-id and request-query-id so we can tie predictions back to logs. We’ll return per-doc scores and confidence buckets.

Costs (rough ballpark):
- For reranking candidates (100 -> top20) with a mid-size model, expect ~0.8–1.5 USD per 1k requests at your traffic profile for PoC (very rough). We’ll produce a refined estimate after we run a small pilot.

Deliverables I can produce this week:
- Offline eval plan + script (python) that computes NDCG/MRR from your export.
- Sample SDK snippet for token exchange and ranking call.
- Canary checklist with rollback thresholds and dashboards.

I’m available for the kickoff Thu May 20, 10:30am PT.

If that works, Kimberly — please go ahead and schedule and I’ll post the internal runbook.

— Rishi
